Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-12-10 15:00 UTC

Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Michael Cho (Redwood Infra); Aisha Khan (Finova CISO), Tom Reynolds (VP Eng), Helen Meyer (Legal), Diego Ruiz (Platform)

Summary (auto-generated):
Finova is evaluating Redwood for an EU-first deployment for their banking product. Primary concerns: strict EU data residency, region pinning for model inference, no cross-border storage of PII, subprocessors (cloud regions) list, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, audit log retention and RBAC/SSO. Discussed Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and routing/fallback behavior. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide region-pinning whitepaper, SCCs, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and architecture diagram for VPC/private deployment; Finova to confirm data classification and legal constraints.

00:00:05 Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick intro then dive into your data residency questions, real quick intros from our side.
00:00:15 Aisha: thanks Samir, I'm Aisha Khan CISO at Finova. Our main ask is EU-only processing for customer-identifiable info - want to understand how Redwood pins requests to EU regions and what happens during failover.
00:00:28 Samir: got it, that's exactly what we'll cover. lena, want to start with the high level routing model?
00:00:33 Lena: sure - so Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted, dedicated, and private. For hosted we have region pinning where you can specify policy to route inference into a given cloud region (e.g., eu-west-1). we also offer dedicated pools and a private VPC option where the control plane can be segregated. in EU-first configs we can prevent any cross-border processing when configured.
00:00:58 Tom: how do you enforce that? is it at the load balancer, or do you actually restrict model replicas to EU?
00:01:05 Lena: good question. enforcement is multi-layered: policy at the routing layer forbids routing to non-EU model instances; model replicas can be pinned to physical hosts in EU zones; and the orchestration layer uses placement constraints. there is also a network-level control for private deployments where egress is blocked to non-EU destinations.
00:01:26 Diego: what about temporary cache or kv cash - like prefix cache - could that end up in US?
00:01:31 Lena: we have automatic prefix/KV caching, and for EU-only tenancy we ensure caches are placed in EU. apologies if transcript said KV cash earlier - it's KV cache.
00:01:40 Aisha: okay, and storage - logs, transcripts - we cannot have PII leave EU or be stored in US. how's that handled?
00:01:49 Michael: for hosted we retain logs per region and can limit retention and residency. for customers with strict requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools in EU and control over snapshotting; Private gives you full control over control plane and storage endpoints so you can point to EU-only S3 or on-prem storage.
00:02:10 Helen: do you offer customer-managed keys (KMS) so keys never leave EU?
00:02:16 Lena: yes - we integrate with regional KMS providers; for cloud KMS we support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed keys when required. for Private deployments you can bring-your-own-key in your EU account and Redwood will use the key for encrypting at rest and for object storage encryption.
00:02:33 Aisha: and is there any chance that during failover you fall back to a US region model and process EU traffic there?
00:02:41 Samir: short answer: we provide policy-based fallback controls. you can configure hard pinning (no cross-border fallback allowed) or soft pinning (attempt EU first, then fallback to other regions if capacity constrained). if you select hard pinning and we can't meet capacity, requests fail with a clear error rather than crossing borders.
00:03:00 Tom: how do you handle legal mechanisms for cross-border processing if we ever need to permit it - standard contractual clauses?
00:03:07 Samir: yes, Redwood provides SCCs (standard contractual clauses) and DPA templates; we'll share the latest SCC pack and our sub-processor list. but for customers that mandate no cross-border processing, we strongly recommend Private or Dedicated in EU.
00:03:20 Helen: need to see the actual sub-processor list and whether any vendors have US access. also need retention windows on audit logs for at least 7 years for some controls.
00:03:31 Priya: quick note - we already have a published sub-processor list and SOC 2 and ISO artifacts; Samir will attach redacted reports.
00:03:39 Aisha: another thing: SSO - we require SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and RBAC controls so only certain roles can call inference endpoints that touch PII. can you do token-level RBAC?
00:03:51 Lena: yes - we integrate SAML/SSO and support SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based across the console and API keys; you can create scoped API keys limited to models or routes. also audit logs track token usage and API calls with timestamps.
00:04:06 Diego: is there a way to separate dev/test traffic to non-prod models outside EU? we want EU prod only, dev can be global.
00:04:13 Samir: yes - per-route policies and model pinning allow you to route production routes into EU-only pools and dev/test routes elsewhere. that's a common pattern.
00:04:24 Tom: what about model weights - if I bring an LLM or you host an open model, are model files or checkpoints ever transferred out of EU?
00:04:31 Lena: for Hosted EU-first we pin model artifacts to EU storage; for BYO models in Private we respect your storage localization. for Dedicated, we manage model artifacts within your EU cluster unless you opt-in to cross-region replication.
00:04:46 Aisha: subprocessors - do you use any inference accelerators or third-party graph services based in US?
00:04:52 Michael: our primary cloud hosts in EU are aligned with major cloud providers; our subprocessor list includes providers with EU datacenters. we do use telemetry and observability backends, but for EU-only customers we can limit or disable cross-border telemetry shipping. we'll send the current list that shows locations.
00:05:10 Helen: please note we need an attestation that no employee outside EU can access EU customer data by default. is that possible?
00:05:18 Samir: we can provide controls and contractual commitments; for emergency access we have just-in-time access controls, logging, and customer notice. for highest assurance customers we recommend Private with VPC and customer-controlled KMS.
00:05:32 Aisha: okay, on the technical side - when you say region pinning, if a user in EU hits our app, and it calls Redwood hosted eu-west-1, is the TLS termination in EU as well?
00:05:44 Lena: yes TLS termination is regional; the entire request path stays within the specified region for region-pinned configs.
00:05:50 Tom: what about model fallback to smaller quantized models that might only be located in US to save cost?
00:05:56 Lena: model variants can be hosted per-region; we don't automatically relocate model variants across regions. fallback to a cheaper model in another region would only happen if you allow cross-border fallback; otherwise we choose same-region compatible variants.
00:06:10 Diego: are there monitoring endpoints that still call US endpoints for alerting?
00:06:14 Michael: monitoring can be configured - for EU-only customers we can route monitoring/alerts to EU endpoints or disable external telemetry; we will document defaults.
00:06:25 Helen: legal question - do you sign DPA with EU SCCs as-is? or do you expect customer redlines?
00:06:31 Samir: we provide a standard DPA and SCCs; many customers request redlines and we work with legal. we also have an EU-specific offering for stricter data residency terms.
00:06:41 Aisha: encryption in transit and at rest - do you support TLS 1.2/1.3 and AES-256?
00:06:47 Lena: yes, TLS 1.2/1.3, and at-rest encryption is AES-256. for BYOK we integrate with KMS and HSM; keys can be region-scoped.
00:06:56 Tom: what about audit log retention and access - can we get read-only access to raw logs?
00:07:02 Priya: we can export logs to customer-owned S3 or syslog endpoints. many customers pull logs into their SIEM. we can also push Redwoods' audit logs to EU storage per retention policy.
00:07:12 Helen: need to see sample audit log schema - timestamps, request ids, model id, requester identity, route, response size, token counts.
00:07:20 Lena: we'll attach sample schema - includes request_id, route, model_version, token_usage, user_id (if provided), and response hashes; we can omit PII fields from logs or redact them.
00:07:31 Tom: are there any subprocessors in the US with potential access to EU data during maintenance windows?
00:07:37 Michael: we try to avoid that; maintenance access is controlled and audited. we'll provide the sub-processor list with country locations and access model.
00:07:46 Aisha: one more: cross-border caching - content-addressable caches that replicate across regions for performance - do you use that?
00:07:54 Lena: not for EU-pinned configs. global caching is disabled; caching is regional.
00:08:02 Diego: okay, about latency - if we force EU-only and we have limited dedicated capacity, will you queue requests or fail?
00:08:10 Samir: depends on policy - hard pin returns capacity errors; soft pin will queue or route to burst capacity within EU if available. Dedicated gives guaranteed capacity.
00:08:19 Tom: related: pricing differences if we choose EU-only Dedicated vs global Hosted?
00:08:24 Samir: Dedicated is contracted reserved capacity with monthly commits; price per token often lower at scale but with commit; EU-only hosting can be slightly higher due to regional premium. we'll include pricing scenarios in the follow-up.
00:08:37 Helen: what about support for data subject access requests (DSAR) - delete all processed PII for a user; can you provide deletion proofs?
00:08:45 Lena: we support data deletion endpoints and can provide logs showing deletion actions, along with snapshots of storage pruning. for stronger guarantees use Private deployment where you control underlying storage.
00:08:58 Aisha: any certifications specific to EU? like ISO 27001 in region?
00:09:03 Samir: Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II and is working on ISO 27001; we have customers in EU and maintain EU data centers. we'll share current certificates.
00:09:12 Tom: ok can you outline how a typical EU-only pilot would look?
00:09:18 Samir: yes - 1) sign DPA + SCCs, 2) set up EU-only account/pinning and scoped API keys, 3) provision dedicated EU pool or private VPC depending on needs, 4) run benchmarks (we can run agent-driven load) 5) evaluate logs and controls - Lena will lead the technical setup.
00:09:36 Lena: for the pilot we'll provide an architecture diagram showing model replicas, KV cache placement, KMS integration, and network egress rules.
00:09:44 Diego: if we do a private deployment on-prem, are there any sub-processors still relevant?
00:09:49 Michael: with on-prem there's minimal Redwood-managed subprocessors; we still have support tooling and control plane, but that can be arranged in an EU-managed control plane for higher assurance.
00:09:59 Helen: we need a statement about legal basis for processing - will Redwood accept controller-to-processor terms in the DPA?
00:10:05 Samir: yes, we operate as a processor and sign DPAs. we'll coordinate legal review.
00:10:11 Aisha: any certifications about employee background checks or access controls for those handling production systems?
00:10:17 Priya: we have standard background checks for engineers; access is role-based and requires MFA. we'll include a short security operations note.
00:10:26 Tom: question on sub-processors - do you use any US-based model inference accelerators (like specialized hardware providers) that require sending data to US?
00:10:34 Lena: not for EU pinned; we can avoid those providers. if you require a specific accelerator we can discuss a dedicated setup in EU.
00:10:42 Aisha: okay great. Helen, any legal follow-ups?
00:10:45 Helen: I'd like to see SCCs, the latest sub-processor list, and the DPA. also evidence of SOC 2 auditor and any ISO artifacts.
00:10:54 Samir: will send all of that.
00:10:57 (short pause)
00:11:10 Tom: on technical controls - can we get read-only access to raw inference logs for compliance audits?
00:11:16 Michael: yes we can set up log exports to your EU S3 with access controls, or a SIEM integration via secure peering.
00:11:25 Diego: is there a standard retention policy? we need at least 7 years in some cases. can retention be set per log type?
00:11:31 Priya: retention is configurable per tenant and per log type; default is 90 days but we can extend and export for long-term archival.
00:11:40 Aisha: what about data residency for embeddings - we generate embeddings for user texts, are vectors considered PII?
00:11:48 Lena: embeddings can be treated as derived data; whether they are PII depends on usage. we recommend treating embeddings as sensitive and applying the same residency rules; we support pinning.
00:12:00 Tom: how about redaction - can you redact PII from requests before storing logs?
00:12:06 Lena: we have pre-processing hooks and redaction pipelines; you can configure to strip PII before logs are persisted.
00:12:15 Helen: from legal perspective, want to make sure sub-processors do not have right to repurpose customer data - is that in your DPA?
00:12:21 Samir: yes the DPA restricts sub-processor use to providing the services and prohibits repurposing. we'll provide a copy.
00:12:29 (transcription glitch) Speaker 4: mmm...
00:12:35 Aisha: can we get an attestation for EU-only admin access?
00:12:39 Michael: we can scope admin access and create region-limited admin roles; for full assurance, Private deployments with customer-managed control plane are best.
00:12:49 Tom: what about disaster recovery - if EU region is down, what is the RTO and do backups ever leave EU?
00:12:57 Lena: DR is region-aware - for EU-only you can choose mirrored EU region DR (e.g., eu-west-1 to eu-central-1). backups remain in-region unless cross-region replication is enabled. RTO depends on committed SLA; Dedicated/Private tiers have SLA options.
00:13:14 Diego: cost of DR?
00:13:16 Samir: DR replicates storage and standby capacity - we'll include cost estimates in the follow-up.
00:13:23 Helen: audit trail - can we get tamper-evident logs?
00:13:28 Lena: we can provide append-only audit logs with integrity checks and export to your archival store; we also support SHA hashes for evidence.
00:13:39 Tom: one more about subprocessors - any use of US-based support engineers who could access debugging data?
00:13:45 Priya: support access is logged and can be restricted; we also offer just-in-time privilege escalation with customer approvals.

00:17:18 Samir: SCCs + DPA are standard; BCRs are less common for service providers but we can discuss alternative transfer mechanisms.
